hsm.title: Highway Safety Manual
hsm.decided: critical rate against the corridor's own sites (user, #34 item 7, docs/03); used in every state until that state's own screening is built

crash_costs.page: Table 1 'Utah's Crash Costs for Calendar Year 2026 (2025 Dollars)', p. 1; rule 'Application of Severity Distributions and Crash Cost Values' 2, pp. 3-4
rules: UDOT: 'Apply weighted crash costs when working with observed crash severities', so K and A crashes are each priced at the weighted KA (Severe) cost, $3,904,059, not at K $15,593,700 and A $1,661,800
UDOT's costs are per crash and already account for multiple people hurt in one crash (memo p. 2)
U (injury, level not reported) unpriced; Utah's layer has no U rows

statewide_rates.missing: UDOT's crash-cost memo and HSIP manual (June 2025) give no statewide average crash rates by facility type, and CrashIQ has no Utah traffic counts

screening.state_method: UDOT ranks HSIP projects by benefit-to-cost ratio from crash history, statewide crash models of the state system and usRAP (UDOT HSIP Manual, June 2025, Sec. 5.1.2.1 and 5.1.3, pp. 14-15)

min_years.missing: UDOT's documents read here set no minimum study period for a corridor study
